description: A low, bulb-forming (corm) perennial about 15-25 cm tall with narrow grass-like leaves and violet flowers with three bright red stigmas. The flowers bloom in autumn, and each flower yields only a few stigma threads, which are hand-picked and dried.
cultural_significance: Saffron is the world's most precious spice and is prized in Kashmir, where it is a GI-tagged crop of Pampore. In India it is used in sweets, tilak, festivals and temple offerings, and in the Unani and Ayurvedic traditions as a tonic.
habitat: Dry, sunny temperate regions with well-drained, calcareous soils and cold winters; Pampore in the Kashmir Valley is the main Indian growing area.

uses.title: Skin complexion and glow
uses.detail: Kumkuma is described as Varnya; mixed in milk or ointments it is traditionally used on skin.

uses.title: Cold, cough and respiratory complaints
uses.detail: Strands in warm milk are a traditional remedy for colds and chest congestion.

uses.title: Mood and calm
uses.detail: Clinical trials suggest saffron extract may help mild-to-moderate low mood; research is promising but not conclusive.

uses.title: Menstrual comfort
uses.detail: Traditionally used for painful or irregular menstruation; avoid in pregnancy.

uses.title: Tonic and rasayana use
uses.detail: Described as Tridoshahara and used as a general tonic and for nourishing the heart (Hridya).

preparations.name: Kesar doodh (saffron milk)
preparations.method: Soak a few strands in warm milk for several minutes.

preparations.name: Kumkumadi taila
preparations.method: Classical medicated oil containing saffron and other herbs.
preparations.note: Traditionally applied on the face; made by manufacturers.

preparations.name: Kumkuma lepa
preparations.method: Grind a few strands with water or milk.

preparations.name: Saffron tea
preparations.note: Light use only, due to expense and potency.

precautions: Large amounts (several grams) are toxic and can cause vomiting, dizziness and bleeding; saffron in medicinal quantities may stimulate the uterus and should be avoided in pregnancy. Use caution with blood pressure and sedative medicines. Allergy is possible. Beware of adulteration (dyed threads, safflower, turmeric).

cultivation.climate: Dry temperate with cold winters; 5-25 C
cultivation.harvest: Flowers hand-picked in autumn; stigmas separated and dried

conservation_status: Not threatened as a crop; it is sterile and propagated only by corms. Kashmiri production has declined in recent years.
fun_fact: It takes about 150,000 flowers to make a kilogram of saffron, which is why it is so costly.

regions.name: Iran & Central Asia
regions.note: Iran produces most of the world's saffron
